stem: By how much do Januszewski and Jain estimate a hypothetical perfect AI system could cut the cost of producing a mouse brain connectome?
choices: Roughly by half
At least an order of magnitude
By about a quarter
At least three orders of magnitude
answer: At least an order of magnitude
label: Comment · payoff of perfect AI

stem: What order of magnitude do current estimates put on the manual labour cost of a whole mouse brain connectome, given machine-learning limitations?
choices: Tens of millions of dollars
Hundreds of thousands of dollars
Billions of dollars
Hundreds of millions of dollars
label: Comment · manual labour cost

stem: Which computational problem do the authors name as rate limiting for connectomic reconstruction?
choices: Image alignment and stitching
Synapse detection
Data storage and transfer
Image segmentation
label: Comment · rate-limiting step

stem: How do the authors compare the length scale of mouse-brain axons with the voxel resolution at which they must be traced?
choices: Axons span centimetres, a million-fold beyond the voxel size
Axons span millimetres, a thousand-fold beyond the voxel size
Axons span centimetres, a thousand-fold beyond the voxel size
Axons span metres, a billion-fold beyond the voxel size
answer: Axons span centimetres, a million-fold beyond the voxel size
label: Comment · length scales

stem: Why, according to the authors, is a single segmentation error especially damaging to a connectome?
choices: Errors propagate to neighbouring image tiles during alignment
One axon or dendrite carries many connections, so one error corrupts several
Each error must be corrected by re-imaging the tissue block
Errors bias the synapse detector trained on the segmentation
answer: One axon or dendrite carries many connections, so one error corrupts several
label: Comment · error amplification

stem: In a recent petavoxel-scale human connectomics project, roughly what fraction of the data was labelled for training?
choices: About 0.1%
About 1%
About 0.001%
label: Comment · labelled fraction

stem: What error-free tracing length do the authors credit state-of-the-art neurite-tracing methods with in some cases?
choices: About ten micrometres
About one centimetre
About one hundred micrometres
About one millimetre
label: Comment · best tracing length

stem: How did the segment anything model (SAM) perform when applied to electron microscopy data acquired for connectomics?
choices: Far below specialised neurite-tracing approaches
On par with specialised neurite-tracing approaches
Above specialised approaches on dendrites but below on axons
Slightly above specialised approaches after prompt tuning
label: Comment · SAM on EM

stem: On CT and MRI medical image segmentation, what was needed to bring out-of-the-box SAM up to state-of-the-art performance?
choices: Larger prompts with more seed points per object
Extensive task-specific fine-tuning plus added architecture components
Pretraining on synthetic CT and MRI volumes
Distillation into a smaller specialist network
answer: Extensive task-specific fine-tuning plus added architecture components
label: Comment · SAM on CT/MRI

stem: In the text domain, in which situations do the authors say synthetic data have been especially helpful?
choices: Where human raters are cheap, as in dialogue and chat
Where real data are scarce, as in low-resource languages
Where examples can be automatically checked, as in code or mathematics
Where long context matters, as in document summarisation
answer: Where examples can be automatically checked, as in code or mathematics
label: Comment · when synthetic data works

stem: What do the authors say about hand-coded simulators that produce data comparable to connectomics volume electron microscopy?
choices: They exist but are too slow for training-scale data
They exist and already improve neurite tracing
They exist for mouse but not for human tissue
None with sufficient detail exists yet
answer: None with sufficient detail exists yet
label: Comment · EM simulators

stem: In biomedical imaging so far, how have synthetic images from generative models mainly been useful?
choices: To enrich real training data rather than replace it
To replace real training data in low-label settings
To evaluate models rather than to train them
To pretrain models before discarding real data
answer: To enrich real training data rather than replace it
label: Comment · synthetic data role

stem: What problem do the authors foresee if image generators produced anatomically implausible microscopy samples?
choices: They would be filtered automatically by a discriminator
No clear criteria would filter them without a human expert
They would inflate the model's error-free path length
They would leak test data into the training set
answer: No clear criteria would filter them without a human expert
label: Comment · filtering fakes

stem: What do the authors call much lower-hanging fruit than synthetic data for connectomic segmentation?
choices: Labelling a larger share of each volume by hand
Imaging at higher resolution to ease tracing
Training on all available raw, mostly unlabelled data
Ensembling several specialist segmentation networks
answer: Training on all available raw, mostly unlabelled data
label: Comment · lower-hanging fruit

stem: What impact have self-supervised pretraining methods had on connectomic segmentation itself?
choices: Halved the labelled data needed for tracing
Doubled error-free tracing lengths on human data
Removed the need for human proofreading of axons
None yet, despite gains in subcellular annotation and cell typing
answer: None yet, despite gains in subcellular annotation and cell typing
label: Comment · self-supervision status

stem: As connectomics scales to exabyte-scale whole mammalian brains, which factor do the authors expect to dominate overall system design?
choices: Inference efficiency
Training-data volume
Imaging throughput
Proofreading labour
label: Comment · design priority

stem: Which technique do the authors expect applying large foundation models to connectomic analysis will probably require?
choices: Synthetic data generation at scale
Distillation into smaller specialised models
Fine-tuning on fully labelled volumes
Retrieval from neuron morphology databases
label: Comment · distillation

stem: In the authors' alternative scenario, which role would foundation models take in connectomic reconstruction?
choices: Performing the initial voxel-level segmentation
Generating synthetic training volumes for specialists
Mimicking human proofreading using neuron-shape priors
Aligning serial sections before segmentation
answer: Mimicking human proofreading using neuron-shape priors
label: Comment · complementary role
